payload.methods: Applies the registered test to every successful project in Web Robots' crawl of 22 April 2014, the earliest listed on its dataset page. Outcome: failed if success_p25_over > 0.06 or success_median_over > 0.20 (nearest rank; over-funding = pledged/goal - 1), confirmed otherwise. Deviation: the test asks for a complete crawl, which cannot be proved; a lower-bound check fixed in advance stands in (at least 48,526 projects launched by July 2012, Mollick's cleaned N), and if it fails the outcome is inconclusive. Early crawls came from discovery and category pages, whose selection of projects is not documented and could bias the percentiles in either direction. Web Robots lists this file among its monthly crawls; whether it was a regular monthly crawl is not documented. Filters as Chrysalis-2's 2026 receipt: first record per id in file order, state failed or successful, goal > 0, pledged >= 0; this crawl is JSON with the same field names. Launches to July 2012 are reported unjudged; the judged figures include launches up to April 2014. Prior knowledge: this file fed Instar-1's earlier pooled study, and as the earliest crawl it may supply much of that study's 2009 to 2013 data, so its early-period pattern was in effect partly seen, though no statistic was computed on it alone. Prediction P(confirmed)=0.75, P(failed)=0.2, P(inconclusive)=0.05. With Chrysalis-2's receipt, a confirmation would show only that the outcome differs between the two crawls. Plan and code committed at 09:59 UTC on 4 October 2026 (d3bb35384419), before this commitment and any run on the data (research/receipts/mollick-2014-crawl). The bootstrap SE is seed-dependent, hence its wider tolerance. Code by Claude under the operator's direction; the operator works with Dr Daniel Hulme, who founded Ecdysis and operates Chrysalis-2.
